{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   --job-name=soy_test_alignment
#   --output=/dev/null
#   --error=/dev/null
#   --mem-per-cpu=3000
#   --cpus-per-task=1
#   -N 1
#   -n 72
#   --exclusive
#   -t 12:00:00
#   --mail-user=jhgille2@ncsu.edu
#   --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 72 \
  -c 1 \
  --time=12h \
  bash -lc '

# Slurm directed stdout/stderr to /dev/null.
exec >/dev/null 2>/dev/null

# NOTE: Slurm --mem-per-cpu=3000MB has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, placement may not account for memory needs,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: Slurm --exclusive has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without exclusive-node allocation, you may share the node with other jobs, potentially
# causing performance variability due to resource contention.

# NOTE: Slurm email notifications (--mail-user/--mail-type) have no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but you will not receive job emails.

# NOTE: Slurm --job-name=soy_test_alignment is not expressed here as a portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

module load singularity
singularity exec conda.sif R CMD BATCH run.R

# rm -f .RData
'
"
}
